statements.status_notes: RUSTSEC-2026-0372 is an informational unmaintained-crate notice for zvariant_derive; it does not identify a specific exploitable defect. The published uv/uvx payload reports this crate in its embedded dependency inventory. uv 0.13.10 enables Linux Secret Service keyring support through secret-service 5 and zbus 5. The standalone crate has no patched version; its replacement is part of zbus 6. secret-service 6.0.0 supports zbus 6, but changes the runtime and cryptography features used by uv. Migration and compatibility validation in uv remain under investigation. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0372.html and https://github.com/open-source-cooperative/secret-service-rs/releases/tag/v6.0.0.

This is an informational unmaintained notice for the standalone zvariant_derive crate. In uv 0.13.7, zvariant_derive 5.11.0 is a procedural-macro library ([lib] proc-macro = true). Its implementation runs on the build host during compilation and is not linked into the installed uv or uvx executables. This assessment covers the macro crate only, not the separate zvariant or zbus_names runtime crates. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0372.html and https://docs.rs/crate/zvariant_derive/5.11.0/source/Cargo.toml.

NiFi ships the prebuilt uv binary from astral-sh/uv release 0.13.5 at /home/nifi/.local/bin/uv. The finding is in uv's embedded Rust dependency tree; remediation requires a newer uv release that updates the affected crate versions. No fixed zvariant_derive release is published yet.

RUSTSEC-2026-0372 is an informational notice that zvariant_derive is unmaintained as a standalone crate, not a specific security vulnerability. uv includes it transitively through secret-service and zbus 5.15 for Linux keyring support. No patched standalone release exists; remediation requires an upstream dependency migration to zbus 6 and remains under evaluation.
